name: Crate of Lightforge Ingots
summary: The Crate of Lightforge Ingots contains rare consecrated metal recovered to forge an instrument capable of defeating the necromancer Morbent Fel. Packed securely for transport, it is destined for the anvils of the Dwarven District in Stormwind.

sections.title: A Sacred Delivery
sections.body: Lightforge iron is an exceptionally rare material, inherently suited to channel holy power against dark entities. Packed away securely in this crate, the ingots represent the hope of Duskwood in its bitter struggle against the Scourge necromancer Morbent Fel, whose shadowy protections shrug off ordinary steel. Ordinary smiths cannot simply work with this metal; it takes an artisan who understands its temper and respects its sacred nature.

sections.title: The Weaponsmith of Stormwind
sections.body: The crate is meant for Grimand Elmore, a skilled dwarven weaponsmith plying his trade in the Dwarven District of Stormwind. Having not worked with lightforge iron in years, Grimand agrees to hammer the metal into a sanctified weapon—an arm imbued with the strength needed to shatter Morbent Fel's defenses and strike him down.

faq.answer: The crate holds ingots of lightforge iron, a special consecrated metal gathered to craft a weapon specifically designed to pierce the magical defenses of the necromancer Morbent Fel.

faq.q: Who is supposed to receive this crate?
aliases: who do i bring the crate to
faq.answer: The crate must be brought to Grimand Elmore, a seasoned dwarven smith located by the anvils of the Dwarven District in Stormwind.
The necromancer Morbent Fel shields himself with vile unholy magic that repels conventional blades. Lightforge iron holds sacred properties that can pierce through dark sorcery.
The raw lightforge ore was collected from the wilderness and securely boxed up so an adventurer could safely deliver it to a master weaponsmith in Stormwind.

angles.text: Working with lightforge iron is a rare art; even veteran weaponsmiths like Grimand Elmore go years without laying hands on such resonant, holy metal.
These ingots are uniquely receptive to the Holy Light, making weapons forged from them natural banes against necromancers and their undead minions.
